description: Used `cd` into projects/ai-certification to rebuild the stage-4 certification zip, then made further Bash tool calls without cd'ing back to the IES project root. The shell's persisted working directory stayed inside the subfolder, so the next UserPromptSubmit hook invocation resolved `.claude/hooks/eval-turn-start.py` relative to the wrong directory and failed with No such file or directory. David confirmed this is the 3rd time this exact pattern (bare `cd` into a subdirectory to build a zip, never returning to project root) has happened.
correction: Never use a bare `cd` when the only reason to change directory is to build a zip file. Always use `(cd subdir && zip ...)` in a subshell so the persistent Bash working directory never leaves the project root, regardless of how the zip command succeeds or fails. This applies specifically and permanently to any zip-building command, not just as a one-off preference.
systemic_fix: Treat 'bare cd before a zip command' as a hard rule violation going forward: zip operations must always be wrapped in a `(cd dir && zip ...)` subshell. This is now a confirmed recurring failure (3rd occurrence), not an isolated slip — should be added as a standing rule/checklist item (e.g. a CLAUDE.md note or git/skill-level guardrail) rather than relying on in-context memory alone.
